;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**[[Azerbaijan]]'s second-largest city [[Ganja, Azerbaijan|Ganja]] is [[shell (projectile)|shelled]] by [[Artsakh Defence Army|Artsakh forces]], destroying several buildings and killing at least one civilian. [[Ganja International Airport]] is also bombed. Azerbaijani [[Ministry of Defence (Azerbaijan)|Defence Minister]] [[Zakir Hasanov]] says it is a "clearly provocative" move that was "expanding the conflict". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-54407436 (BBC News)]
**The [[Republic of Artsakh|Artsakh]] capital [[Stepanakert]] is struck with [[Multiple rocket launcher|MLRS]] missiles resulting in heavy casualties and leaving the city without power. Artsakh President [[Arayik Harutyunyan]] warns major cities in Azerbaijan are now "legitimate targets of the defence army" following the strikes on Stepanakert. [https://eurasianet.org/armenia-azerbaijan-fighting-expands-far-beyond-the-front-lines (Eurasianet)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-54407436 (BBC News)]
**[[Azerbaijani Land Forces|Azerbaijani troops]] reportedly seize control of the city of [[Cəbrayil]] (Jabrayil) from Artsakh forces. [[Armenia]] denies the city has fallen. [https://ahvalnews.com/nagorno-karabakh/azerbaijani-forces-take-city-jabrayil-they-make-territorial-gains-nagorno-karabakh (Ahval News)]
**Azerbaijan says medium-range missiles have hit its [[Khizi District|Khizi]] and [[Absheron District|Absheron]] districts, as well as the city of [[Mingachevir]]. [https://apa.az/en/frontline-news/Hikmet-Hajiyev:-Armenians-launched-two-300-km-mid-range-missile-in-Khizi-and-Absheron-regions-332077 (APA)]
*[[Terrorism in Germany]], [[Antisemitism in 21st century Germany]]
**An [[2020 Dresden knife attack|attack by an Islamic extremist]] kills one tourist and injures the other. The suspect was later arrested. [https://www.reuters.com/article/germany-security-suspect-int-idUSKBN2772B9 (Reuters)]
**Amid the [[Jewish holidays|celebration]] of [[Sukkot]], a 26-year-old [[Jews|Jewish]] student suffers a [[traumatic brain injury]] after being attacked with a shovel by a 29-year-old German Kazakh man as he entered a [[synagogue]] in [[Hamburg]]. [[Hamburg Police|Police]] later discover a piece of paper with a [[swastika]] on it in one of the attacker's trouser pockets. [[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Germany)|Foreign Minister]] [[Heiko Maas]] denounces the attack as "repugnant [[antisemitism]]". [https://www.timesofisrael.com/man-reportedly-attacks-jewish-student-with-shovel-outside-hamburg-synagogue/ (AFP via ''The Times of Israel'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema]]
**[[Cineworld]] announces it is temporarily shutting down all its [[movie theater|cinema]]s in the [[United Kingdom]] and [[United States]], putting more than 5,500 jobs at risk, after reporting [[pound sterling|£]]1.3bn in losses since the [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]] lockdown. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-54407213 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Five people who went missing during heavy [[flood]]s in [[France]] two days ago are found dead in river banks in the [[Italy|Italian]] [[regions of Italy|region]] of [[Liguria]], while a man is found dead at [[France-Italy border|the border]] between the two countries. Italy is also affected by floods. A man has died in his car during the floods in the French region of [[Saint-Martin-Vésubie]].  [https://www.ilfattoquotidiano.it/2020/10/04/maltempo-trovati-5-cadaveri-in-liguria-tra-i-detriti-della-mareggiata-in-zona-non-sono-stati-segnalati-dispersi-allerta-in-emilia-per-il-po/5953734/ (''Il Fatto Quotidiano'')] [https://www.lunion.fr/id195775/article/2020-10-04/intemperies-dans-les-alpes-maritimes-un-homme-retrouve-mort-saint-martin-vesubie (L'Union)]
*A [[multiple-vehicle collision]] on a main road in [[Fuyu, Jilin]], [[China]], kills 18 people. [[Ministry of Public Security (China)|Police]] say an inquiry is under way into the cause of the accident. [https://news.sky.com/story/china-road-crash-18-killed-after-minivan-hits-tractor-and-then-collides-with-car-12089546 (Sky News)]
*Eight migrants are dead, while 12 more are missing, after three unidentified smugglers hijacked their boat off the coast of [[Djibouti]], according to eyewitnesses and the [[International Organization for Migration]]. The agency reports that the migrants had attempted to reach [[Saudi Arabia]] via [[Yemen]], but were forced to return to the [[Horn of Africa]] due to [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic-related travel restrictions]]. [https://www.macaubusiness.com/8-migrants-dead-12-missing-off-djibouti-coast-iom/ (AFP via Macau Business)]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] surpass 100,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/news-pmn/crime-pmn/polands-total-number-of-coronavirus-cases-exceeds-100000-2 (Reuters via ''National Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 10,499 new cases in the past 24 hours, setting a record for the highest number of daily new cases since May 15, when the outbreak was at its peak and lockdowns were in place in parts of the country. This is also the first time that daily new infections surpassed 10,000 since May. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/russia-records-over-10000-coronavirus-cases-for-1st-time-since-may (''Daily Sabah'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The United Kingdom surpasses 500,000 cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] after a backlog of infections left out of [[Public Health England]]'s daily figures between September 25 and October 2 led to a record 22,961 cases reported in 24 hours. The glitch led to 15,841 cases not being passed on to data dashboards used for contact tracing. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/04/delay-in-reporting-uk-coronavirus-cases-risks-further-spread-say-scientists (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*The Presidents of [[Palau]], [[Nauru]], [[Kiribati]], the [[Federated States of Micronesia]] and the [[Marshall Islands]] issue a statement threatening to leave the [[Pacific Islands Forum]] if their nominee is not chosen as Secretary-General. Micronesian [[President of the Federated States of Micronesia|President]] [[David W. Panuelo]] says the issue is "non-negotiable". [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/427562/micronesian-nations-to-withdraw-from-forum-if-concerns-not-heeded (RNZ)]

;Law and crime

*[[Nigeria]]n Inspector General of [[Nigeria Police Force|Police]] [[Mohammed Adamu]] bans the [[Special Anti-Robbery Squad]] and other tactical units from engaging in stop-and-search operations at traffic stops and from setting up roadblocks, as well as mandating that all police officers wear uniforms while on-duty, in response to mounting allegations of agents unlawfully arresting and torturing suspects. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/4/nigeria-special-police-reined-in-over-abuse-allegations (Al Jazeera)] 

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 New Caledonian independence referendum]]
**New Caledonians reject independence from France with 53.26% of votes, according to final results. Turnout is reportedly high. [[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] welcomes the result as a "sign of confidence in the republic". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-54410059 (BBC News)]
*[[October 2020 Kyrgyz parliamentary election]]
**[[Elections in Kyrgyzstan|Parliamentary elections]] are being held in [[Kyrgyzstan]] amidst an [[economy of Kyrgyzstan|economic]] crisis. [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-kyrgyzstan-election-idUKKBN26P004 (Reuters)]
*The [[Mali]]an interim [[government of Mali|government]] releases 110 [[jihadist]]s from their [[Bamako]] prison after releasing 70 yesterday. It is believed that their release is part of a [[prisoner exchange]] to secure the release of opposition politician [[Soumaïla Cissé]], who was kidnapped earlier this year. [https://apnews.com/article/mali-archive-prisoner-exchange-6ef5691bdbe75fa000c01a30a6c9ed8e (AP)]
